summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Tom Allen had skipped out to Windsor, Ontario, to avoid prosecution in Kentucky over the Goss fight, after failing to appear on $1,000 bail given in Chicago.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Sunday Morning, November 12, 1876, page 7

facts.fact: Allen fled to Windsor, Ontario, to avoid prosecution for violating Kentucky statutes in the Goss-Allen fight
Allen was arrested in Chicago at the instance of Kentucky officers and gave $1,000 bail to appear before Justice Scully, but failed to appear; his bondsman was Mike McDonald
When arrested, Allen protested that he had no intention of avoiding his trial set for November 20, 1876
Billy Harrison, advance agent of Mace and Allen, was in Cheyenne on his way to California to prepare exhibitions for the two; Mace had also gone west

notes: Needs a recrop and OCR of the 'Tom Allen.' section (column 2, top). Facts read from the low-resolution page image, hence medium confidence. Some believed Allen meant to reach the Pacific coast to escape his Kentucky prosecutors.
